title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
authors: Pritam Das, Satadeep Bhattacharjee, Pil-Ryung Cha
abstract: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.
summary: This paper develops and applies a sophisticated, open-shell projection-based embedding method to study the location of redox holes in $	ext{Li}$-rich layered oxides. By coupling a correlated quantum solver (DMRG) to a DFT environment, the authors find that the hole localizes on oxygen pairs, demonstrating that methodological consistency and geometry control are more critical than the quantum solver itself. This provides a robust framework for calculating electronic structure in complex, strongly correlated solid-state materials.
main_problem: The study addresses the complex, open-shell, and strongly correlated problem of determining where the redox hole localizes in Li-rich layered oxides.
main_result: The hole consistently localizes on an oxygen pair, and the primary source of uncertainty in the results stems from state control and geometry consistency, rather than the correlated solver itself.
method: The authors employ a spin-unrestricted, projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding technique, coupling a small active region solved by a correlated quantum solver (DMRG) to the bulk environment treated by DFT.
model_or_system: The system modeled is delithiated $	ext{Li}_{2-x}	ext{MnO}_3$, a layered oxide cathode material. The calculation involves embedding a small cluster of interest within a larger periodic DFT environment.
key_observables: Hole location (e.g., on oxygen pair), $	ext{O–O}$ bond formation (Mayer bond order), and the magnitude of spin projection errors across the active/environment boundary.
important_parameters: Environment functional (e.g., $	ext{DFT+U}$ vs. $	ext{HSE}06$), geometry, active region size, and the degree of orbital overlap across the embedding boundary.
main_assumptions: The method is formally exact at the DFT-in-DFT level, but the authors note that total energies are not converged at the highest orbital counts, and the choice of environment functional significantly impacts hole characterization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the workflow from periodic calculations to cluster carving and active region partitioning. Figure 2 details the cluster model of delithiated $	ext{Li}_2	ext{MnO}_3$, showing magnetization density and the nested active regions.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical formalism of the open-shell projection-based embedding, applies this formalism to $	ext{Li}_{2-x}	ext{MnO}_3$ using DMRG-in-DFT across various parameter variations, and concludes by analyzing the sources of computational uncertainty.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of simulating strongly correlated materials by rigorously testing advanced embedding techniques necessary for accurate prediction of redox chemistry in solid-state batteries.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Workflow of this study. Periodic calculations locate the holes and supply geometries and point charges (1); clusters are carved around the hole-bearing oxygen pair (2); a global unrestricted Kohn–Sham (UKS) calculation is converged for each of seven environment functionals with an explicit state search (3); the occupied space is partitioned per spin by SPADE into nested active regions, with the active-space spin projection fixed by rule A (4); the embedded problem is solved by non-spin-adapted DMRG with unrestricted orbitals (5a) or, in a device-sized active space, by sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) with an unrestricted subspace solver (5b).
